nanaimo-gabriola-island-mla--sheila-malc.summary: MLA for Nanaimo-Gabriola Island since 2024 (Nanaimo, 2019–2024) and Minister of Social Development and Poverty Reduction since 2022. Previously MP for Nanaimo–Ladysmith (2015–2019) and chair of the Islands Trust Council.

nanaimo-gabriola-island-mla--mark-macdon.summary: Owner of a media and public relations company, former co-publisher of the Business Examiner and former managing editor of the Nanaimo Daily News. Past president of the Greater Nanaimo Chamber of Commerce.

nanaimo-gabriola-island-mla--anna-mary-m.summary: Cree journalist, policy advisor and child and youth advocate based in Nanaimo, and a Jack Webster Award recipient. Board member of tâpwêmin media and advisor with Spotlight: Child Welfare.

nanaimo-lantzville-mla--george-anderson.summary: MLA for Nanaimo-Lantzville since 2024 and Parliamentary Secretary for Transit. A lawyer, he served on Nanaimo city council and the Regional District of Nanaimo board (2011–2014) and has chaired VIU's board of governors.

nanaimo-lantzville-mla--kelsey-pringle.summary: Co-founder and owner of a B.C. digital marketing agency. Board member of the Vancouver Island Economic Alliance and co-founder of Empower Women Canada, which supports women entrepreneurs.

victoria-beacon-hill-mla--grace-lore.summary: MLA for Victoria-Beacon Hill since 2020. Previously Minister of Children and Family Development and Minister of State for Child Care, and a political science instructor at the University of Victoria.

victoria-beacon-hill-mla--rajinder-sahot.summary: Lawyer and managing partner of a firm focused on personal injury, human rights and class actions. Longtime board member of Pacifica Housing Advisory Association and a youth soccer and basketball coach.

victoria-beacon-hill-mla--joachim-agou.summary: Professional engineer in defence-sector test and evaluation and owner of a Victoria engineering consulting and media company. Previously worked at MDA and MDS Aero; interim vice-president of the Victoria Conservative Association.

victoria-swan-lake-mla--nina-krieger.summary: MLA for Victoria-Swan Lake since 2024 and Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General since 2025. Previously executive director of the Vancouver Holocaust Education Centre.

victoria-swan-lake-mla--carolyn-howe.summary: Teacher at South Park Family School since 2005 and president of the Greater Victoria Teachers' Association since 2024. Also a choral conductor and performer.

victoria-swan-lake-mla--tim-taylor.summary: Licensed real estate professional, property manager and strata manager in Victoria. Has chaired the Victoria Real Estate Board's commercial division and the Kiwanis Housing Society for Seniors.

esquimalt-colwood-mla--darlene-rotchford.summary: MLA for Esquimalt-Colwood since 2024 and Parliamentary Secretary for Labour. Previously an Esquimalt councillor, a mental health and addictions worker, and a labour leader.

esquimalt-colwood-mla--dave-johnston.summary: Red Seal electrician from Colwood who served over a decade as a Canadian Ranger and managed capital projects for the Haisla Nation. Founder of The North Matters, a resource-development advocacy nonprofit.

esquimalt-colwood-mla--sidney-coles.summary: Freelance journalist, including two years as a Local Journalism Initiative reporter with Capital Daily. Former Ontario public servant who has worked as communications manager for the Gitanyow Hereditary Chiefs.

esquimalt-colwood-mla--sid-tobias.summary: Mayor of View Royal since 2022 and a Capital Regional District director. Canadian Armed Forces veteran of nearly 25 years and former B.C. public servant.

conservative-party.blurb: Describes itself as an independent provincial party built on limited, fiscally responsible government, individual liberty, a free-enterprise economy and private property, alongside a social safety net for vulnerable people.

bc-green-party.blurb: Describes itself as North America's oldest Green party, founded in 1983, guided by sustainability, participatory democracy, social justice, ecological wisdom, non-violence and respect for diversity.

centrebc.blurb: Describes itself as a pragmatic, moderate option focused on affordability, safety and opportunity, favouring evidence-based decisions, public services backed by a strong private sector, and elected officials finding common ground.

onebc.blurb: Describes itself as on a mission to lower taxes, defend families, reform democracy, preserve the environment, and deliver world-class health care, education and public infrastructure.

communist-party-of-bc.blurb: Describes itself as offering an anti-monopoly, working-class platform to strengthen the rights of working people, Indigenous peoples and the environment.
communist-party-of-bc.note: No About page found; wording taken from the party's platform page.

christian-heritage-party-of-bc.blurb: Describes itself as standing on a foundation of individual dignity, personal freedoms, economic enterprise and limited government, which it says are granted by the Creator.
